source.original_feedback_text: Overall a good attempt, however, in Scenario 1, while the use of Or.elim is valid, the proof concludes eligibility after only one of the two conditions is met, bypassing the requirement that both a prerequisite and an approval are needed; this results in an incomplete formalisation. Scenario 2 displays sound reasoning and structure, but uses by_contradiction, causing the proof to fail at the compilation level. Scenario 3 is well-handled, compiling successfully and using constructive reasoning across both disjunctive cases in a manner faithful to the task. In Scenario 4, the proof attempts to validate a different implication than the one required. In Part 2, theorems 1 through 3 are correct, demonstrating clean application of the provided axioms. Theorem 4 follows the correct logical idea but fails to compile due to an implicit argument error in AxConjIntro, likely from how the contradiction is structured.

Scenario 1 contains an incomplete formalisation, Scenario 2 has a compilation failure despite sound reasoning, Scenario 4 proves a different implication from the one required, and Theorem 4 follows the correct logical approach but fails to compile because of an AxConjIntro implicit argument error.
